Hypergeometric functions

Source: R/hyper.R
hypergeometric-functions.Rd

The confluent and Gauss hypergeometric functions, with the kernels scipy.special uses (Boost.Math for real hyp1f1, as in SciPy).

Usage

sc_hyp0f1(v, z)

sc_hyp1f1(a, b, x)

sc_hyp2f1(a, b, c, z)

sc_hyperu(a, b, x)

Arguments

v, a, b, c

Numeric vectors of parameters.

z, x

Numeric vector; complex too, except for sc_hyperu().

Value

A double vector, or a complex vector for complex input.

Details

  • sc_hyp0f1(): \({}_0F_1(;v;z)\), complex.

  • sc_hyp1f1(): Kummer's \({}_1F_1(a;b;x)\), complex x.

  • sc_hyp2f1(): the Gauss \({}_2F_1(a,b;c;z)\), complex z.

  • sc_hyperu(): Tricomi's \(U(a, b, x)\) for real x >= 0.

Only the last argument may be complex; the parameters are real. Arguments are recycled, NA gives NA, and the result takes its dimensions, or else its names, from the arguments as base R arithmetic does; see sc_seterr() for the conditions the kernels raise.

Branch cuts

sc_hyp2f1() has a branch cut on the real axis from 1 to infinity, as in SciPy. sc_hyp0f1() and sc_hyp1f1() are entire in z.

Other packages

In gsl, for real arguments: hyperg_0F1(), hyperg_1F1(), hyperg_2F1() and hyperg_U(). In hypergeo: hypergeo(A, B, C, z), the Gauss function for complex z.

See also

https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/special.html#hypergeometric-functions

Examples

sc_hyp0f1(0.5, 1)
#> [1] 3.762196
sc_hyp1f1(1, 2, c(0.5, 1 + 1i))
#> [1] 1.297443+0.0000000i 1.378025+0.9093307i
sc_hyp2f1(1, 1, 2, 0.5)
#> [1] 1.386294
sc_hyperu(1, 2, 3)
#> [1] 0.3333333
